summary_html: Family agrees to a **voluntary service plan**—counseling, substance-use treatment, parenting classes—designed to correct conditions without court compulsion. Federal law prioritizes family preservation through prevention and support services.
authority_html:
- **Family First Prevention Services Act (FFPSA)** — prevention services and kin support framework  
- **SSA Title IV-B (42 U.S.C. §§ 620–629m)** — child-welfare services and family-preservation funding

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that an order placing a family under informal supervision pursuant to Welfare and Institutions Code section 360(b), without declaring the child a dependent, is tantamount to a disposition and is therefore appealable, and it affirmed the juvenile court's orders on the merits.
key_cases.relevance: Is the California authority describing the section 360(b) informal supervision program, the court-adjacent route by which a family receives services without being declared dependents.
key_cases.quote: We therefore construe the order of the juvenile court for informal supervision under section 360, subdivision (b) as a disposition order.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed jurisdictional and dispositional orders entered after a mother who asked her physician for help with cocaine use was referred to the agency, holding the juvenile court did not abuse its discretion in declaring the child a dependent rather than ordering family maintenance services under section 360(b).
key_cases.relevance: Shows that voluntary, agency-supervised family maintenance under section 360(b) is a lesser alternative the court must consider but is not required to choose.
key_cases.quote: The court has broad discretion to determine what would best serve and protect the child's interest and to fashion a dispositional order in accord with this discretion.

state_agency.name: California Department of Social Services

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.deadline: Detention hearing no later than the next judicial day after the dependency petition is filed; petition due within 48 hours of custody, excluding nonjudicial days
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Child must be released from custody (Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code §§ 313, 315)
